tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.

details.bpSpecification: Blue, crystalline powder or transparent, blue crystals.

tests.procedure: Weigh 100 mg sample in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min, repeat shake/hold once if not dissolved; stepwise add 0.9 mL, 2 mL, 7 mL solvent (same shake and hold) to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved use 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble) then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble. Repeat with methanol and ethanol (96 per cent).

details.reference: BP (SC IV K.) Characters Section (Hygroscopicity and Solubility)

tests.procedure: Identification test 1: add several drops of dilute ammonia R2 to 1 mL of solution S; a blue precipitate forms; on further addition of dilute ammonia R2 the precipitate dissolves and a dark blue colour is produced.

details.reference: BP 2022 Monograph for Copper Sulphate pentahydrate

tests.procedure: Identification test 3 (sulfates): dilute 1 mL of solution S to 5 mL with water; add 1 mL dilute hydrochloric acid and 1 mL barium chloride solution R1; a white precipitate is formed.

details.reference: BP Appendix VI, Qualitative Reactions and Tests, Sulfate

tests.procedure: Appearance of solution: compare solution S with water; solution S is clear.

details.reference: BP Appendix IV A, Clarity of Solution

tests.procedure: Lead limit by AAS: dissolve 0.5 g in 10 mL water, add 2.5 mL lead-free nitric acid, dilute to 25.0 mL with water. Reference solutions from lead standard solution (10 ppm Pb) with 2.5 mL lead-free nitric acid, diluted to 25.0 mL. Lead hollow-cathode lamp, 217.0 nm, air-acetylene flame. NMT 20 ppm.

details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix VIII T, Determination of Elemental Impurities, AAS

tests.procedure: Nickel limit by AAS: dissolve 0.5 g in 10 mL water, add 2.5 mL lead-free nitric acid, dilute to 25.0 mL. Reference from nickel standard solution (10 ppm Ni) with 2.5 mL lead-free nitric acid, diluted to 25.0 mL. Nickel hollow-cathode lamp, 232.0 nm, air-acetylene flame. NMT 20 ppm.

details.reference: BP Appendix II D, Atomic Spectrophotometry: Absorption

tests.procedure: Cobalt limit by AAS: dissolve 0.5 g in 10 mL water, add 2.5 mL lead-free nitric acid, dilute to 25.0 mL. Reference from cobalt standard solution (0.5 ppm Co) with 2.5 mL lead-free nitric acid, diluted to 25.0 mL. Cobalt hollow-cathode lamp, 240.7 nm, air-acetylene flame. NMT 1 ppm.

details.reference: BP Appendix II D, Atomic Spectrophotometry: Absorption

tests.procedure: Chlorides limit test (BP Appendix VII): 10 mL solution S diluted to 15 mL with water, add 1 mL dilute nitric acid, pour into a tube with 1 mL silver nitrate solution R2; standard 10 mL chloride standard solution (5 ppm Cl) and 5 mL water with 1 mL dilute nitric acid treated the same way. After 5 min protected from light, opalescence of the test not more intense than the standard (NMT 100 ppm).

details.reference: BP Appendix VII Limit Tests, Chloride

tests.procedure: Iron limit by AAS: dissolve 0.5 g in 10 mL water, add 2.5 mL lead-free nitric acid, dilute to 25.0 mL. Reference from iron standard solution (20 ppm Fe) with 2.5 mL lead-free nitric acid, diluted to 25.0 mL. Iron hollow-cathode lamp, 248.3 nm, air-acetylene flame. NMT 100 ppm.

details.reference: BP Appendix II D, Atomic Spectrophotometry: Absorption

tests.procedure: Loss on drying (BP Appendix IX D): weigh empty weighing bottle previously dried at 250 ± 10 °C and cooled in desiccator (W0); weigh 1.000 g sample (W1); dry in calibrated oven at 250 ± 10 °C for 2 h, cool in desiccator, weigh (W2); repeat to constant weight. % LOD = (W1 - W2) / (W1 - W0) x 100.

Assay (iodometric titration): dissolve 0.200 g sample in 50 mL water; add 2 mL sulfuric acid and 3 g potassium iodide; titrate with 0.1 M sodium thiosulfate, adding 1 mL starch solution towards the end. 1 mL of 0.1 M sodium thiosulfate = 24.97 mg CuSO4·5H2O. Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100) / Wt.

details.titrantStandardization: 10.0 mL of 0.033 M potassium bromate + 40 mL water, 10 mL potassium iodide solution, 5 mL hydrochloric acid R1; titrate with thiosulfate with starch added near the end (1 mL = 2.783 mg KBrO3)
details.indicator: 1 mL starch solution, added towards the end of the titration
details.equivalenceFactor: 1 mL of 0.1 M sodium thiosulfate = 24.97 mg CuSO4·5H2O
details.formula: Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100) / Wt; E.P = end point (mL); eq.wt = equivalent weight of copper sulfate pentahydrate; F = titrant factor; Wt = sample weight (g)
details.reference: BP Appendix VIII D (as cited in STM)
details.basis: as stated (no basis word on the STM)
